text:
Will Cuylle has become the Rangers' Swiss Army knife, as Sports Illustrated put it, and the New York Post wrote about him showing off that flexibility with an eye on his next contract. The tools are easy to see: 85 hits in 23 games, a top-line chance rate (1.35 expected goals per 60), and Evolving-Hockey had him taking chances away at a 94th percentile rate last season.

What hasn't caught up is the scoreboard. He has 6 goals on 8.62 expected, and the Rangers have scored 4.7 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. That costs him both ways: fewer goals and fewer assists. He keeps getting the looks, and goals tend to follow chances. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he gets 2.2 shots per 60 off the most dangerous passes, which makes the drought look more like bad luck than bad hands.

Our range has him at 16 to 29 goals. The middle of that, plus the hitting, is a player the Rangers will want to keep.
